strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 benchmarks, 3 model families, and multiple model sizes with consistent improvements (+1.5-2.8% accuracy, +56-79% token efficiency)
Well-motivated problem formulation clearly articulating limitations of pure explicit and pure latent reasoning
Training-free design enabling practical deployment without retraining, with clear algorithmic description and implementation details supporting reproducibility
Asymmetric mode-switching design (immediate L→E, delayed E→L) is well-reasoned based on the different roles of exploration vs. consolidation
Particularly strong results on harder benchmarks (AIME: +5% on Qwen3-1.7B), showing the method benefits problems with higher uncertainty
Extensive supplementary results including detailed performance at varying token budgets, pass@k analysis, and thorough ablation studies
weaknesses: Limited novelty: core contribution (entropy-based switching between modes) is relatively straightforward and primarily combines existing techniques; concurrent work (Liang et al. 2025) observes similar stochasticity benefits

Insufficient baseline comparisons: only compares against CoT variants and Soft Thinking; missing evaluations against recent concurrent training-free latent reasoning methods and adaptive thinking approaches mentioned in related work

Weak justification for entropy-based switching: entropy of next-token distributions may be noisy and unreliable confidence indicators; no analysis of switching failure modes or empirical validation that switches align with intuition

Incomplete mechanism analysis: no visualization/statistics of actual switching patterns, no analysis of which problems benefit/suffer from switching, missing error analysis and investigation of why latent reasoning helps in low-confidence regions
High hyperparameter sensitivity: β₀ ablation shows extreme variance (8.33% to 61.55%); paper exposes α₀ to users for manual adjustment, complicating deployment; W_E→L requires dataset-specific tuning

Limited evaluation scope: restricted to mathematics and STEM reasoning only; Pass@k experiments only on one model; small AIME test sets (30 problems) with only 8-run averaging and no confidence intervals or significance tests
Token efficiency gains weaker on harder problems where accuracy gains are larger, suggesting an accuracy-efficiency trade-off that limits practical impact on challenging reasoning tasks

Design choices lack empirical justification: thinking-related signal mixing with scheduled α_t, β_t appears ad-hoc; convergence/termination triggers via injection queues are heuristic; no ablation comparing entropy to simpler confidence metrics

strengths: Clear problem formulation identifying two concrete limitations of latent reasoning (probability mass diffusion and overthinking)
Practical, training-free method with elegant entropy-based switching criterion and asymmetric dwell window design
Comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple benchmarks (5), model families (3), and scales (3 sizes)
Extensive ablation studies systematically validating design choices (window size, signal mixing, convergence triggers)
Substantial token efficiency improvements (56-79%) under constrained budgets with Pass@k analysis showing 50% fewer samples needed
Well-organized reproducibility support including detailed Algorithm 1, hyperparameter tables, and supplementary experiments across broader domains
weaknesses: Limited novelty: entropy-based confidence estimation and switching between reasoning modes based on uncertainty are relatively straightforward ideas lacking theoretical justification
Modest accuracy improvements on unlimited budgets (1.5-2.8% average), with negligible gains on easier benchmarks (GSM8K: +0.46%, MATH500: +2.40%)
Entropy as confidence measure lacks theoretical grounding—no exploration of alternative signals (max probability, probability margins) or justification for why entropy is optimal

Hyperparameter complexity contradicts simplicity claims: β₀ causes dramatic sensitivity (AIME2024: 8.33%-50.83%), WE→L requires tuning, α₀ is task-dependent; this undermines the 'drop-in replacement' framing
Small improvements over main training-free baseline (Soft Thinking): +2.03% for Qwen3-8B, +2.68% for Qwen3-1.7B; weak explanations for why SWIREASONING outperforms
Identified but unresolved limitations: spatial reasoning tasks requiring rigid constraints fail due to inherent 'smoothing vs. precision' trade-off in latent reasoning (Appendix C.6)
Large efficiency gains partly reflect early stopping via switch count control rather than inherently better reasoning; efficiency metric interpretation (4.6x-6.8x) should be treated cautiously

Shallow mechanistic analysis: while Figure 6 shows latent modes provide diversity, unclear which problem types benefit from latent vs. explicit modes or when switching helps—largely descriptive rather than explanatory
